The problem asks for the area of an equiangular octagon.
An equiangular octagon has all interior angles equal.
The sum of interior angles of an $n$-gon is $(n-2) \times 180^\circ$.
For an octagon, $n=8$, so the sum is $(8-2) \times 180^\circ = 6 \times 180^\circ = 1080^\circ$.
Since it is equiangular, each interior angle is $1080^\circ / 8 = 135^\circ$.
The exterior angles are $180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ$.

Let the side lengths be $s_1, s_2, \dots, s_8$ in counterclockwise order.
The condition "no two consecutive sides have the same length" implies that the lengths must alternate.
So the sequence of side lengths must be $1, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 1, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 1, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 1, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
